name: Robben Island Lighthouse
scope: Separately research the lighthouse on Minto Hill and its exact anchor. Do not place it at the island story reference point.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

review.method: Expired-copyright dated photographic postcard and primary museum/firsthand architectural text; native mapped circle and independent ground retained.
review.notes: Full surviving lighthouse tower accepted at the agreed approximate medium-fi scope. Local Qualla images and saved category decisions were checked first; no eligible lighthouse photograph was available there. The dated Walsh photographic postcard, demonstrably in postal circulation by1911, is public domain by expiry and was inspected as an exact crop of its1987grayscale reproduction. It supports the circular taper, base/door, staggered openings, projecting gallery, raised glazed lantern and domed cap. Robben Island Museum independently describes the white18metre circular masonry tower on Minto Hill. Architect William Martinson’s firsthand written2019site description supplies the measured21.25m base circumference, east door/daymark, eight shaft sash windows, curved main-gallery rails, second lantern gallery, sixteen alternating tapered glazed panels and twelve-part curved metal cap. Lighthouse fact-file text independently identifies the black east stripe and red lantern. No private modern photograph is active. Existing geometry agrees with these controls and native mapped circle. Minor window/door profiles, precise opening levels, paint tones, gallery/ladder dimensions and optical equipment remain explicit approximations. Original tower-only scope retained; office, engine room, former keeper cottage, landscaping and interiors remain excluded. Map anchor, heading, independent ground, source/runtime/four LODs and fourteen portable/shared render bytes remain unchanged. No reference pixels embedded.

originalReview.notes: Entire selected postcard inspected at native reproduced resolution. The complete lighthouse shows circular tapered shaft, base and doorway, staggered recessed openings, projecting curved gallery and raised lantern/gallery, glazed drum, domed cap and vane. Old keeper cottage is outside the unchanged modern tower scope. Historic grayscale reproduction gives no current paint control.
